cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and his brother Aaron, the priest. This time the subject is the human body. Buckle up, friend, because Leviticus does NOT do small talk.

cards.question: Who are Moses and Aaron supposed to pass this message on to?

cards.text: Here's the first case. When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.

cards.question: True or false: a man's discharge only makes him unclean while it's flowing.

cards.text: And it doesn't stay with him. Any bed he lies on and any furniture he sits on becomes unclean too.

cards.question: Someone touches the bed of the man with the discharge. What must that person do?

answers.text: Wash his clothes and bathe with water
Shave off all his hair and his beard
Stay outside the camp for a whole week

cards.question: After washing and bathing, the one who touched the man's bed will be unclean until ___.

cards.text: Sit where he sat, touch his body, or get spit on by him, and it's wash, bathe, unclean until evening, every single time. Friend, in that camp your clothes got washed MORE than they got worn.

cards.question: Even when the man with the discharge goes riding, any ___ he rides on will be unclean.

cards.text: Whoever touches or carries anything that was under him gets the same routine. Then the law gets to his hands.

cards.question: The man with the discharge touches someone. When does that person have to wash and bathe?

answers.text: When he didn't rinse his hands first
When he touched them after dark
When he touched them on the Sabbath

cards.text: Now the law walks right into the kitchen. And friend, as a kitchen tool myself, I am holding my BREATH.

cards.question: Any clay pot the man with the discharge touches must be ___.
True or false: a wooden utensil the man with the discharge touches must be broken too.

cards.text: Then the good news: the man is cleansed from his discharge, and now he starts counting. Believe me, I know counting. I counted the dust in a junk drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: The cleansed man counts off ___ days for his cleansing, washes his clothes and bathes in fresh water.

cards.text: On the eighth day, he comes before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. And he brings two birds for the priest.

cards.question: What two birds does the cleansed man bring to the priest?
The priest sacrifices the man's two birds. What are they offered as?

answers.text: A sin offering and a burnt offering
A guilt offering and a grain offering
A peace offering and a wave offering

cards.text: In this way the priest makes atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge. He isn't left stuck, friend. The way through is written right there.
Next comes a shorter case. When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water.

cards.question: True or false: after an emission of semen, the man brings two birds to the priest on the eighth day.

cards.text: Any clothing or leather with semen on it gets washed with water and stays unclean until evening. Then the law covers a man and a woman together.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, only the man has to bathe.

cards.text: Now the law turns to women. When a woman has her flow of blood, she is unclean due to her menstruation.

cards.question: A woman is unclean due to her menstruation for ___ days.
During a woman's period, what happens to anyone who touches her?

cards.text: Anything she lies or sits on during her period is unclean. Touch her bed or her furniture, and the laundry's back: wash, bathe, unclean until evening.

cards.question: True or false: if a man lies with a woman during her period and her flow touches him, he is unclean only until evening.

cards.text: Then a different case. A woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her period, or it keeps going past it.

cards.question: How long is a woman with this kind of discharge unclean?

answers.text: All the days of her discharge

cards.text: Her bed and furniture are unclean, just like during her period. Anyone who touches them washes, bathes and is unclean until evening.

cards.question: A woman's discharge stops and she is cleansed of it. What comes next?

answers.text: She bathes and is clean that evening
She goes straight to the priest

cards.text: On the eighth day, she heads to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Sound familiar? Same doorway the man went to.

cards.question: On the eighth day, the cleansed woman brings the priest two turtledoves or two young ___.
True or false: the priest sacrifices the woman's birds and makes atonement for her before the LORD.

cards.text: Then God gives the reason behind all of this. Lean in, friend, this is the big one.

cards.question: Why must the children of Israel be kept separate from their uncleanness?

answers.text: So they don't die by defiling His tabernacle
So sickness doesn't spread through the camp
So the nations around them take notice

cards.text: The law wraps up by naming every case: the man with a discharge, the emission of semen, the woman's period, any discharge, and a man who lies with an unclean woman. Not one case left out. Told you, Leviticus does NOT do loose ends.

findings.problem: The whole passage is purity rules, many of them repeated case by case (touching a bed, sitting on furniture, being spit on, riding a saddle, carrying things, each with the same wash, bathe, unclean until evening routine). That looks like the long-stretch categories 'rules for everyday life' and 'repeated reports'. The walkthrough treats them in full detail across two stops and puts many choice cards on them (for example the saddle, until evening, and the clay pot). The docs say a long stretch gets one summary card, no choice cards and never a stop of its own. They also say key laws and teaching are not long stretches. They don't say what to do when an entire passage is regulations.
findings.question: When a whole passage is a list of everyday or ceremonial rules, like Leviticus 15, should the long-stretch rule apply to its repeated cases, so only the distinct cases and the reason in 15:31 get choice cards? Or should the whole passage count as teaching or key law and be walked through in detail?

findings.problem: Most of stop 1's choice cards can't be reasoned out from the earlier cards. They are discovery questions: card 4 (flowing or blocked), card 6 (what someone who touches the bed must do), card 7 (until evening), card 9 (saddle), card 16 (seven days), card 18 (which birds) and card 19 (which offerings). The story cards before them give no context that points to the answer.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The card says whoever touches anything that was under him 'gets the same routine', which card 8 set up as wash, bathe, unclean until evening. Leviticus 15:10 only says the one who touches will be unclean until evening. Washing clothes and bathing is required only of the one who carries such things.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Then the law gets to his hands' points straight to the one answer on card 11 that mentions hands ('When he didn't rinse his hands first'), so the two wrong answers are ruled out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card tells a beat from Leviticus 15:11 (the law getting to his hands) but cites only Leviticus 15:10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'They're unclean for seven days' can be argued from Leviticus 15:24. There, a man who lies with her and is touched by her flow is unclean seven days, so a baker could argue that touching her can bring seven days of uncleanness.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: No story card sets up Leviticus 15:24. Card 7 has just taught that touching her means unclean until evening, so a thoughtful baker reasoning from the earlier cards would pick True. Only luck or prior knowledge gets this one right.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'Told you, Leviticus does NOT do loose ends' calls back to something he never said. Stop 1 card 1 said 'Leviticus does NOT do small talk', not anything about loose ends.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.
